stumbles.quote: Colours match a reference to mean ΔE76 0.07.
stumbles.why: The text never says what the reference is (a photo? a physical film? a spectral model?). It also doesn't say what was compared. ΔE76 is jargon to many developers, and 0.07 is far below a visible difference, so the claim is hard to judge.

stumbles.quote: Not yet tried on a real phone.
stumbles.why: This conflicts with the pitch of tilting the phone. It leaves unclear whether the tilt interaction has ever been tested, and whether the demo is meant for phones or desktops.

stumbles.quote: It drains at the border, goes black from the top, then pops.
stumbles.why: "It" is only implied to be the film. "Goes black" is unexplained, and it is not obvious that this means thinning to nothing before the film bursts. "The border" is also unclear: it could be the frame or the screen edge.

point: A WebGPU compute-shader soap film demo that you tilt like a phone so thick film sinks and thin film rises, then drains, blackens and pops. Its colours are said to closely match a reference, but it hasn't been tested on a real phone.
